options: A short, structured document describing a model's intended use, training data, evaluation, and limitations
A credit card issued to the data science team
A physical label attached to a server rack
A one-time sign-off email sent before deployment
questions.explain: A model card is a structured, repeatable document — not a one-off email or a physical object — that answers the same set of questions for every model.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say the 'out-of-scope use' section often prevents incidents rather than just explaining one afterward?
options: It's the line that stops a model built for one purpose from quietly getting reused for a decision it was never validated on
It lists the model's file size and storage location
It is required only for models that failed their first evaluation
It replaces the need for an evaluation section entirely
questions.explain: Explicitly documenting what a model was NOT validated for is what stops someone from reusing it for an unrelated, unvalidated decision later.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a section the lesson lists as part of a standard model card?
options: The model's current stock price
Intended use
Known limitations
Training data summary
questions.explain: Models don't have stock prices — the real sections are intended use, out-of-scope use, training data, evaluation, limitations, and owner/review date.

questions.q: Who does a well-written model card need to serve, according to the lesson?
options: Both technical builders/reviewers and non-technical stakeholders like compliance officers or regulators
Only the original author of the model, for their own reference
Only external auditors, never internal engineers
Only end users of the application, never engineers
questions.explain: A card that serves only one audience is incomplete — it needs both the technical detail builders need and the plain-language framing non-technical reviewers need.

questions.q: What happens when a model has no documentation and the person who built it leaves the company?
options: The model's behavior and limitations become effectively unknown to everyone else
The model automatically stops running for safety
Unity Catalog automatically generates a replacement card
Nothing changes, because models don't require maintenance
questions.explain: Without documentation, the model's intended use, data, and limitations exist only in one person's head — once they leave, that knowledge is effectively gone.
